entities.summary:
Likud is Israel’s principal centre-right to right-wing party, formed in 1973 as an alliance consolidating Revisionist Zionist and liberal currents, with headquarters at Metzudat Ze’ev in Tel Aviv. Menachem Begin’s 1977 victory ended decades of Labor dominance and realigned Israeli politics.

Likud coalitions advanced settlement expansion, market liberalisation, and hard-security doctrines while also negotiating landmark diplomacy such as the Egypt peace treaty. Later leaders from Shamir to Netanyahu made Likud the default vehicle of the Israeli right.

As a party institution, Likud transformed Israel from a Labor-hegemonic polity into a competitive system pivoted on nationalist conservatism.
